summary: Analysis of 14 days of Nightscout telemetry reveals overall solid glycemic control with a Time in Range (70-180 mg/dL) of 86.0% and an average glucose of 121.6 mg/dL. However, safety is compromised by high nocturnal hypoglycemia (10.1%-18.5% Time Below Range between 23:00 and 03:00) and substantial afternoon volatility (peak 32.1% Time Above Range at 16:00 followed by 15.3% Time Below Range at 19:00). Zero carbohydrates are logged in Nightscout, forcing AAPS Unannounced Meal (UAM) logic to manage all meal responses. Delayed gastric emptying from GLP-1 agonist therapy causes UAM to accumulate excessive insulin on late meal waves, leading to postprandial drop-offs. Disproportionately high AAPS safety ceilings (Max IOB 25 U, Max Basal 12 U/h) and an overnight target of 90 mg/dL compound these risks.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM data coverage is excellent at 98.7% over 14 days with only 10 minor gaps (largest 65 min). Profile and AAPS settings are complete. Critical gap: complete absence of logged carbohydrate entries (0 g total), forcing total reliance on UAM automation.
analysis_steps.evidence: 3,995 entries out of 4,046 expected; treatment_summary total_carbs_g = 0.0.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of logged carb entries obscures direct evaluation of Carb Ratios (CR) and absorption durations.

analysis_steps.findings: Overall Time Below Range (<70 mg/dL) is elevated at 5.1% (target <4.0%). Hypoglycemia is concentrated overnight (10.1%-18.5% TBR between 23:00-03:00) and early evening (15.3% TBR at 19:00). Severe lows down to 41 mg/dL recorded. Confounding factors include concurrent GLP-1 receptor agonist use (1.25 mg weekly) and pump occlusion events.
analysis_steps.evidence: glucose_summary TBR = 5.1%; hourly_glucose_local TBR at 01:00 = 18.5%, 19:00 = 15.3%; glucose_extremes include 41 mg/dL.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight glucose drifts downward against a 90 mg/dL target, leading to high low-exposure. Early morning/fasting window (05:00-09:00) is highly stable (TIR 95.2%-98.7%), confirming scheduled basal rates (0.7-0.8 U/h) are accurate when uninfluenced by meal IOB. Afternoon glucose swings are meal/UAM driven, not basal defects.
analysis_steps.evidence: hourly_glucose_local average glucose 05:00-07:00 is 99.5-104.2 mg/dL with <5% TBR; overnight TBR peaks at 18.5% at 01:00.

analysis_steps.findings: Profile ISF is flat at 56 mg/dL/U. Dynamic ISF reduces effective ISF down to 27.8 mg/dL/U during hyperglycemia, intensifying loop auto-dosing. DIA of 10.0 hours correctly models exponential decay, but accumulated UAM IOB outlasts delayed GLP-1 meal absorption. Direct CR verification is blocked by missing carb records.
analysis_steps.evidence: loop logs show dynamic ISF scaling from 27.8 to 124 mg/dL/U; therapy_response_windows show strong 120m correction drops (-168 to -178 mg/dL).
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of logged carbohydrate entries prevents isolate verification of CR segments.

analysis_steps.findings: Because no carbs are logged, UAM and SMB always-enabled serve as the sole automated meal response. During delayed GLP-1 meal absorption, UAM delivers continuous microboluses and high temp basals (up to 4.0 U/h) late into the wave, accumulating up to 5.9 U IOB that drives postprandial crashes.
analysis_steps.evidence: representative_loop_statuses show UAM High Boost enacted with IOB up to 5.93 U at 21:09 and 4.73 U at 15:54.

analysis_steps.findings: Safety limits are set dangerously high: Max IOB is 25 U (>125% of Total Daily Dose ~19.7 U), and Max Basal is 12 U/h (15x-24x baseline basal). Dynamic ISF is active at 70% factor. Autosens is disabled. High safety limits rely entirely on secondary oref1 internal maxSafeBasal caps.
analysis_steps.evidence: aaps_profile.smb_settings.raw_settings: max_iob_units = 25.0, max_basal_u_per_hour = 12.0; treatment_summary total insulin = 275.95 U over 14 days (~19.7 U/day).

analysis_steps.findings: Total reliance on unannounced meals creates severe afternoon peaks (average 162.8 mg/dL at 16:00, maximums >280 mg/dL) followed by early-evening lows (15.3% TBR at 19:00). GLP-1 gastric slowing delays peak carb impact, causing loop UAM logic to over-deliver insulin late in the absorption window.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of logged bolus timing relative to actual meal intake.

analysis_steps.findings: No extended carbs (e-carbs) are logged. Post-meal glucose display shows 3-5 hour extended absorption profiles typical of GLP-1 co-therapy. Without explicit carb logging or extended absorption entries, AAPS default carb absorption dynamic ISF over-titrates insulin.
analysis_steps.evidence: treatment_summary extended_carb_entries = 0; hourly_glucose_local postprandial elevation spans 12:00 to 17:00.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No recorded e-carbs or carb absorption durations in telemetry.

analysis_steps.findings: The primary clinical driver of hypoglycemia is an aggressive overnight target (90 mg/dL) combined with unannounced meal insulin stacking under GLP-1 therapy, exacerbated by excessively wide safety limits (Max IOB 25 U, Max Basal 12 U/h). Baseline basal rates are well-tuned during fasting. Recommended sequence: 1) Raise overnight target to 100 mg/dL; 2) Tighten AAPS Max IOB and Max Basal safety limits; 3) Transition to explicit meal carb logging with extended absorption modeling.

strengths: Overall Time in Range (70-180 mg/dL) is strong at 86.0% with a mean glucose of 121.6 mg/dL.
Fasting and early morning glucose stability (05:00-09:00) is exceptional, achieving >95% Time in Range with minimal hypoglycemia.
CGM data quality and coverage are excellent (98.7% coverage over 14 days).
issues: Elevated overnight hypoglycemia risk, with Time Below Range reaching 18.5% at 01:00 and 11.4% at 00:00.
Excessive postprandial glucose volatility in the afternoon (TAR 32.1% at 16:00) followed by sharp early-evening drops (TBR 15.3% at 19:00).
Complete reliance on unannounced meal (UAM) logic due to zero logged carbohydrates, causing UAM insulin stacking under GLP-1 gastric slowing.
Disproportionately wide AAPS software safety limits (Max IOB 25 U vs ~19.7 U TDD; Max Basal 12 U/h vs 0.8 U/h max scheduled basal).

recommendations.title: Raise Overnight Target Setting
recommendations.description: Increase target setting from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL between 23:00 and 08:00 to create a safety buffer against nocturnal hypoglycemia.

recommendations.title: Tighten Max IOB and Max Basal Safety Ceilings
recommendations.description: Lower Max IOB from 25 U to 7.0 U (~35% of TDD) and Max Basal from 12 U/h to 3.0 U/h to prevent runaway automated dosing during UAM or sensor noise.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Raise the overnight target from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL between 23:00 and 08:00 to reduce nocturnal hypoglycemia.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Time Below Range (<70 mg/dL) reaches 10.1% to 18.5% overnight between 23:00 and 03:00. A target of 90 mg/dL provides insufficient safety margin for nocturnal sensor noise and lingering evening IOB.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Monitor overnight glucose for 5-7 days after adjusting target; verify that TBR between 23:00 and 05:00 drops below 4.0%.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Overnight lows are primarily driven by low target (90 mg/dL) and late evening meal IOB rather than excess baseline basal; retain rate while adjusting target.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Max IOB of 25 U is excessive for a ~19.7 U TDD, offering no safety barrier against UAM stacking or sensor errors. Reduce Max IOB to 7.0 U and Max Basal to 3.0 U/h.
Dynamic ISF performs well during high spikes; retain 70% adjustment factor.
Absorption model parameters are standard for oref1 dynamic carb decay.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Transition from total reliance on unannounced meals (UAM) to logging carbohydrates in AAPS prior to meals. Given GLP-1 gastric slowing, combine a modest immediate pre-meal bolus (e.g., 30-50%) with extended carbohydrate (e-carb) entry spanning 3-4 hours to prevent UAM insulin stacking.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: GLP-1 therapy delays postprandial glucose rises. Unannounced meal logic detects this rise late, delivering continuous SMBs and high basals at peak absorption that cause severe postprandial drop-offs (15.3% TBR at 19:00).
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log meal carbohydrates and pre-bolus timing consistently for 7 days to evaluate true Carb Ratio performance.

exceptions.suggestion: Enter carbohydrates explicitly with an extended absorption duration (e-carbs) over 3 to 4 hours rather than letting UAM react unannounced.
exceptions.rationale: Prevents late UAM insulin accumulation that leads to 18:00-19:00 hypoglycemia (15.3% TBR).

exceptions.suggestion: Avoid unannounced late snacks; log carbs explicitly or use a temporary high target if active carbs remain at bedtime.
exceptions.rationale: Prevents stacked evening IOB from driving overnight lows.

implementation_steps: Step 1: Review and update the profile target from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL between 23:00 and 08:00.
Step 2: Adjust AAPS Safety Limits: lower Max IOB from 25.0 U to 7.0 U, and lower Max Basal from 12.0 U/h to 3.0 U/h.
Step 3: Begin explicit carbohydrate logging in AAPS for all major meals, utilizing extended carb (e-carb) entries over 3-4 hours for GLP-1 delayed absorption.
Step 4: Monitor overnight Time Below Range and postprandial glucose stability for 5-7 days before considering any further profile adjustments.
education: GLP-1 receptor agonists slow stomach emptying, causing carbohydrate absorption to spread over 3 to 5 hours rather than 1 to 2 hours.
When meals are unannounced, automated systems like AAPS UAM interpret delayed glucose rises as continuous high demand, potentially over-delivering insulin late in the absorption window.
AAPS Max IOB acts as a crucial safety ceiling; setting it near or above Total Daily Dose removes protective boundaries against sensor noise or insulin stacking.
safety_notes: This analysis is decision-support content only and does not constitute medical advice.
All proposed parameter changes must be independently verified by the user and reviewed with their healthcare team.
Change parameters one at a time and monitor blood glucose closely following any adjustment.
Always maintain accessible rapid-acting carbohydrates for treatment of hypoglycemia.
